2607.06999.title: Physics-guided spatiotemporal neural models for fuel density prediction
2607.06999.paper_summary: This paper presents a physics-guided machine learning (PGML) framework for fuel density prediction, integrating physics constraints and domain knowledge into deep learning models to enhance model accuracy and stability. We explore three deep learning architectures -- ConvLSTM, Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNONet), and Video Vision Transformer (ViViT) -- to model the spatiotemporal evolution of fuel density. Our approach incorporates differentiable physics-informed terms in the loss function, including a mass-conserving fuel transport term and a rate-of-spread estimation. Experimental results, averaged across multiple independent trials, demonstrate that the proposed PGML framework outperforms purely data-driven baselines without physics constraints in both accuracy and stability. This framework enables computationally efficient, physically plausible fire forecasting to support adaptive prescribed burn management.
2607.06999.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文提出了一個物理引導的機器學習（PGML）框架，用於燃料密度預測，將物理約束和領域知識整合到深度學習模型中，以提高模型的準確性和穩定性。<lb/>我們探索了三種深度學習架構——ConvLSTM、Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNONet) 和 Video Vision Transformer (ViViT)——來建模燃料密度的時空演變。<lb/>我們的方法在損失函數中納入了可微分的物理知識項，包括一個質量守恆的燃料運輸項和擴散速率估計。<lb/>實驗結果在多次獨立試驗中取平均，顯示所提出的PGML框架在準確性和穩定性上均優於沒有物理約束的純數據驅動基準。<lb/>該框架使得計算高效且物理上合理的火災預測成為可能，以支持自適應的預定燃燒管理。
